facts.value: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 (Annex 1 to a cover report, Draft v2), tabled at OPDC Audit and Risk Committee on 2 June 2026 for recommendation onward to the OPDC Board. 11-page strategy from Philip Hall (OPDC Head of Finance) presented via London Treasury Limited, the GLA subsidiary. Report originators printed on p11: Philip Hall (OPDC) and James Graham (London Treasury). Every page carries a 'DRAFT' watermark. This IS the substantive treasury paper — carries the treasury position and CFR table (§3.1, p5), the prudential debt limits table (§3.3, p6), the MUFG interest-rate forecast (§2.7-2.8 Table 1, p5), the year-end resources table (§7.3, p8) and the net financing costs (§8.1, p9). The five appendices listed on p11 (TMPS, MRP Policy, Prudential Code Indicators & Limits, TMPs Main Principles, LTLF Investment Strategy) are named but NOT bundled in this PDF.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: OPDC is a Mayoral Development Corporation established under the Localism Act 2011, not a council. §1.2 (p1) states plainly: 'OPDC's activities within the scope of the TMSS are the investment of cash balances via the GLA and borrowings from the GLA for capital purposes (OPDC has no other borrowings). OPDC's day-to-day cash requirements are funded by the GLA based on need.' §4.3 (p1) confirms MDCs are EXCLUDED from the requirement to charge MRP under Regulation 1(3A)(b) of the Local Authorities (Capital Finance and Accounting) (England) Regulations 2003 — so OPDC does not make MRP, a material difference from every council in our library. Meeting has passed (today is 2026-08-16). No forward treasury-specific committee date is printed in the paper — the paper was for recommendation to the OPDC Board, whose approval date is not in this paper.

facts.value: External Long term borrowing £204.7m at forecast 2025-26 outturn, held FLAT at £204.7m across every forward year in the plan (Budget 2026-27, Plan 2027-28, Plan 2028-29). Finance lease liabilities £1.4m (fcst 2025-26) running down to £1.1m / £0.8m / £0.5m across the forward years. Gross debt £206.1m / £205.8m / £205.4m / £205.1m across the four years. All external borrowing is INTRA-GROUP from the GLA. No PWLB direct exposure. No LOBOs. No market debt. No bank loans.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.value: NOT APPLICABLE. OPDC is not a direct PWLB borrower. Ran: --find 'OPDC' → no match; --find 'Old Oak' → no match; --find 'Greater London Authority' → GREATER LONDON AUTHORITY (parent line). Per §1.2, OPDC's borrowings are all intra-group from the GLA, and the GLA is where our PWLB loan file holds the underlying position. This is a structural fact about MDCs and their funding, not a coverage gap in bc-loans. Any 'reconciliation' against OPDC would be meaningless: there are no PWLB loans in OPDC's name to reconcile against.

facts.note: The email should disclose this upfront and honestly — it is not a limitation of our data, it is a structural feature of the OPDC/GLA borrowing relationship. Attempting to quote a GLA loan book back at OPDC would misrepresent whose money it is. Left out of the email in loan-book-style form.

facts.value: £214.6m (Fcst Outturn 2025-26) → £252.6m (Budget 2026-27) → £259.4m (Plan 2027-28) → £233.0m (Plan 2028-29). Two years of growth (+£44.8m, +21%) then a £26.4m drop in year three. The drop in year three is not narrated in the parts of the paper we hold. External borrowing intra-group from GLA £204.7m stays flat across all four years (see loan_book note).

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: §3.1 (p5) Treasury Position table. CFR grows £44.8m over two years then drops £26.4m — likely a scheduled capital receipt, grant, or programme milestone but the paper we hold does not narrate the year-three drop. §3.2 (p6) narrative: 'The treasury position shows that OPDC is forecast to be underborrowed because of an increase in the CFR. The organisation does not have sufficient balance sheet resources to fully meet this requirement through internal borrowing and will therefore need to draw down additional external borrowing from the GLA during 2026-27 and later in the medium term horizon.'

facts.value: TIES 3/4 EXACTLY, 1/4 TO ROUNDING. CFR − Long-term borrowing − Finance lease liabilities = Under/(over) borrowing. Fcst 2025-26: 214.6 − 204.7 − 1.4 = 8.5 (paper prints 8.5) ✓. Budget 2026-27: 252.6 − 204.7 − 1.1 = 46.8 (paper prints 46.8) ✓. Plan 2027-28: 259.4 − 204.7 − 0.8 = 53.9 (paper prints 53.9) ✓. Plan 2028-29: 233.0 − 204.7 − 0.5 = 27.8 (paper prints 27.9) — £0.1m rounding gap, well inside 1dp presentation tolerance. Paper convention: Under/(over) borrowing is positive when debt is BELOW CFR (under-borrowed / internally borrowed).

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: §3.1 (p5). Four-for-four across the horizon. §7.3 (p8) restates the same identity with the sign flipped ((Under)/over borrowing negative when under-borrowed): fcst 2025-26 -8.5, 2026-27 -46.8, 2027-28 -53.9, 2028-29 -27.9. Same numbers, opposite convention across the two tables.

facts.value: Under-borrowed at every year in the horizon. Fcst 2025-26 £8.5m under-borrowed against £69.1m of investable cash (net investor). From Budget 2026-27 onwards the internal-borrowing gap widens to £46.8m / £53.9m / £27.9m while cash balances turn negative (-£13.7m / -£29.8m / -£8.2m). The transition to net cash borrower coincides with the CFR jumping from £214.6m to £252.6m (+£38m in one year).

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: §3.1 and §7.3. The transition point is 2026-27 (this coming year). Small in absolute terms (£13.7m of cash shortfall) but material as a change of state — from net investor to net borrower. §3.2 explicitly links this to the CFR increase requiring more external drawdown from the GLA.

facts.value: Authorised limit £225.0m (fcst 2025-26) rising to £250.0m from 2026-27 and held constant to 2028-29. Operational boundary £215.0m rising to £240.0m. Gross debt £206.1m (fcst 2025-26) sitting inside both limits with £18.9m of authorised-limit headroom and £8.9m of operational-boundary headroom currently. Forward headroom widens to £44.2-£44.9m against the authorised limit and £34.2-£34.9m against the operational boundary across the plan years, because the limits step up by £25m while gross debt stays flat.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.value: Net financing costs £5.8m (fcst 2025-26) → £8.7m (2026-27) → £10.1m (2027-28) → £10.5m (2028-29). +81% across the three-year plan window. §8.1 (p9).

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: §8.1 (p9). Near-doubling is consistent with: (i) CFR growth requiring new intra-group borrowing at current/forward rates that are higher than the historical £204.7m stock; (ii) the switch from net investor (£69.1m cash balances earning c.4%) to net cash borrower (shortfalls of £13.7m-£29.8m); (iii) higher forward Bank Rate/PWLB expected than at the time the historical debt was drawn.

facts.value: Table 1 §2.7 (p5) — MUFG's central case for Bank Rate and 5/10/25/50yr PWLB across 12 quarterly points Jun-26 to Mar-29. Bank Rate 3.75% held through Jun-27, then to 3.50% (Sep-27), 3.25% (Mar-28) holding to Mar-29. 10yr PWLB 5.50% (Jun-26) → 5.30% (Mar-27) → 4.70% (Mar-28) → 4.60% (Mar-29). 25yr PWLB 6.00% (Jun-26) → 5.80% (Mar-27) → 5.20% (Mar-28) → 5.10% (Mar-29). 50yr PWLB 5.80% (Jun-26) → 5.50% (Mar-27) → 5.00% (Mar-28) → 4.90% (Mar-29). Rates are STANDARD PWLB; the certainty version is 20bp lower at every maturity.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: Table heading says 'MUFG Interest rate view – March 2026' but §2.7 narrative is written 'as at the time of writing (May 2026)' — either a stale heading or a rolled-forward central case labelled by its original vintage. §2.8 gives the paper's own market quote: 'the standard rate on new 10 year PWLB loans increasing from 5.34% at the start of March to 6.15% at the 15th May' — i.e. 65bp above MUFG's Jun-26 central case (5.50%) at time of writing, one month before that horizon. §2.7 also notes the market has priced THREE 0.25% Bank Rate increases within 12 months (3.75% → 4.50%), against MUFG's 'hold and eventually cut' central case. Two dated, testable views printed side by side — the paper does not attempt to reconcile them.

facts.value: GAP: 65bp between MUFG's Jun-26 central case for 10yr PWLB standard (5.50%) and the paper's own 15 May 2026 observed market quote (6.15%). On a certainty basis the gap narrows to 45bp (5.95% certainty vs 5.50% MUFG central case). Bank Rate: MUFG says HOLD at 3.75% until Sep-27 then fall; market at time of writing has priced THREE 0.25% RISES within 12 months to 4.50%.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026 (§2.7-2.8)

facts.note: Both figures are the paper's own — MUFG's Jun-26 central case at Table 1, 15 May 2026 market quote at §2.8. The comparison is not our derivation, it is what the paper puts on the same page. This is the substantive market observation in the email.

facts.value: OPDC is IN THE PROCESS of admission to the London Treasury Liquidity Fund LP (LTLF) as a limited partner during 2026/27. Current LTLF limited partners are the GLA, LPFA and other GLA functional bodies — OPDC and OSDC are the two functional bodies not yet admitted. Until admission completes, OPDC's cash is invested via a 'temporary loan to the GLA, which invests the proceeds in their entirety in the LTLF for the sole benefit of OPDC' (§7.10). This transitional arrangement is expected to cease when OPDC is successfully admitted during 2026/27. Investment limit for periods >365 days is £1m (§7.8).

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.value: §6.2 (p7): 'Officers, following an examination of the cash and borrowing balances of the functional bodies within the GLA Group, will consider the use of intergroup transactions, to offer significant savings on borrowing and/or risk management opportunities. Such an examination will be carried out in accordance with liability benchmarking techniques, as recommended by the CIPFA Treasury Risk Management Toolkit for Local Authorities.' Named GLA Group members: London Fire Commission (LFC), GLA, OPDC, London Legacy Development Corporation (LLDC), London Pension Fund Authority (LPFA), Oxford Street Development Corporation (OSDC), Mayor's Office for Policing and Crime (MOPAC).

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: §6.2 (p7). Explicit reference to liability benchmarking as the framework for intergroup optimisation. The framework the paper uses is the same one we point at in the email as a standing inclusion. Full list of GLA family bodies is useful context — some of these would be searchable as their own mg entities (LLDC, LPFA, LFC, MOPAC, OSDC). None likely to be direct PWLB borrowers (all borrow via GLA in the same on-lending model).

facts.value: §4.1-4.7 (pp 6-7). CFO delegated authority to approve borrowing within the Authorised Limit. Authorised to: (a) borrow for capital expenditure within limit, (b) use cash balances for internal borrowing when advantageous, (c) borrow temporarily within limit where prudent (e.g. short-lived cash flow requirements), (d) borrow temporarily ABOVE the Authorised Limit only where the amount of the increased limit represents delayed payment due to OPDC and not received on due date (Section 5 LGA 2003). All borrowing decisions reported to the Audit and Risk Committee at first opportunity.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: §4.1-4.7. Standard delegation. §5 policy on borrowing in advance of need: 'OPDC will not borrow more than or in advance of need purely to profit from the investment of the surplus borrowed' — will consider if within CFR estimate, market timing, alternative funding forms (revenue, leasing, private partnerships), and appropriate interest bases/repayment profiles. §6.1: 'Decisions may be taken to restructure the debt portfolio, by switching from long term debt to short term debt through the early redemption or replacement of loans, so as to either increase long term affordability or adjust maturity profiles for the purposes of managing liquidity and interest rate risks.' — but no historical rescheduling reported and the debt is intra-group from the GLA, so rescheduling is a different exercise here than for direct PWLB borrowers.

facts.value: OPDC DOES NOT MAKE MRP. §4.3 (p1): 'Regulations under the 2003 Act state that local authorities have a duty to make an amount of MRP which it considers to be prudent. Mayoral Development Corporations established under the Localism Act 2011 are explicitly excluded from the requirement to charge a Minimum Revenue Provision under Regulation 1(3A)(b) of the Local Authorities (Capital Finance and Accounting) (England) Regulations 2003.' Appendix 2 (MRP Policy Statement) is listed on p11 but not bundled in this PDF.

source.title: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 — Annex 1 (Draft v2), OPDC Audit and Risk Committee, 2 June 2026

facts.note: This is a material structural difference from every council we have read. MRP is the mechanism by which most councils' CFR amortises against revenue over time. Without MRP, OPDC's CFR moves only through capital expenditure additions and capital-financing receipts/grants — no automatic year-on-year run-off. This may explain why the paper's £204.7m external borrowing is modelled flat: no principal repayment is scheduled on the historical intra-group facility.

officer.subject: Your paragraph 2.8, priced at certainty — and the 65bp above your Jun-26 view
officer.body:
Dear Philip,

Apologies for the cold email — PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're a small platform that carries PWLB rates at both fixings each working day, monthly local-authority-to-local-authority lending, every local authority's PWLB loan book, and a lightweight academy for treasury officers. The data side is free and stays free. The one-page brochure is at pwlbtoday.com/brochure if it helps to circulate internally.

To keep the data and training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every authority in the country, so we can see how each authority's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. Below are some thoughts on your Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 (Annex 1, Draft v2) as tabled at the 2 June Audit and Risk Committee. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. The paper is short, unusually clean, and this is offered in that spirit rather than as a critique.

One thing to be honest about upfront. OPDC is the first Mayoral Development Corporation we've read, and your §1.2 is explicit that OPDC's borrowings are all intra-group from the GLA rather than direct from PWLB. So our loan-book file cannot hold OPDC — the parent PWLB line is under the GLA, and that is where the direct exposure sits. The loan-by-loan reconciliation we run against most authorities is therefore not applicable to you; it is a structural feature of the MDC funding model rather than something we could fix on our side. Where we can still add something is against the figures the paper does print.

Your §3.1 balance-sheet identity ties across the horizon. CFR minus long-term borrowing minus finance lease liabilities equals your Under/(over) borrowing line: at forecast 2025-26, 214.6 − 204.7 − 1.4 = 8.5 (you print 8.5); at 2026-27, 252.6 − 204.7 − 1.1 = 46.8; at 2027-28, 259.4 − 204.7 − 0.8 = 53.9; at 2028-29 the arithmetic lands at 27.8 against your 27.9 — inside the £0.1m rounding tolerance of a 1dp table. Three exact ties, one on-the-rounding. That is the check we always run first on a treasury paper and it is unusual for it to come out this clean across the whole horizon.

Where the paper opens something up for the market comparison is §2.8. You quote the PWLB standard 10-year rate rising from 5.34% at the start of March to 6.15% at 15 May 2026. That is a standard-rate move; PWLB borrowers on the certainty rate (which the GLA is) pay 20bp less at every tenor, so the 15 May equivalent on certainty terms is around 5.95%. Our page at pwlbtoday.com/pwlb-activity carries both fixings daily against a rolling history if it helps to keep the drift live for the next drawdown decision.

The larger observation is against the MUFG central case in Table 1 (§2.7). MUFG has the 10-year PWLB at 5.50% for Jun-26 and Bank Rate held at 3.75% until Sep-27 before falling. The 15 May 2026 market quote you print at §2.8 is 65bp above that Jun-26 central case — 45bp on a certainty basis — one month before the forecast horizon. §2.7 also notes the market has priced three 0.25% Bank Rate rises within 12 months (i.e. Bank Rate to 4.50%) against MUFG's hold-and-eventually-cut view. Printing both alongside each other is a piece of transparency that we don't see on every strategy, and it is what makes the observation available at all. Whichever view proves out will be answered by observation over the coming quarters — and against the CFR trajectory in §3.1 (£214.6m rising to £252.6m in 2026-27 alone, with net financing costs going from £5.8m to £8.7m over the same year per §8.1) the drawdown timing of new intra-group borrowing is the thing the two views most directly bear on.

The academy is a paid product. Three sessions relevant to what you've tabled: a Prudential and Treasury Code refresher (the CIPFA 2021 Codes are cited at §1.2), a Liability Benchmark walkthrough (the framework §6.2 flags for intergroup optimisation across the GLA family), and a session on the practical mechanics of PWLB standard vs certainty pricing. Free account sign-up is at pwlbtoday.com/sign-up; the new-account discount runs until end of September.

If any of this lands, word of mouth is how we get in front of colleagues elsewhere — a mention to peer treasurers inside the GLA family, or to any Board colleague in the network, would do more than any campaign we could run.

Best,
[NAME]
PWLBtoday
[LinkedIn]

Sources: OPDC Treasury Management Strategy 2026/27 (Annex 1, Draft v2), tabled at OPDC Audit and Risk Committee 2 June 2026, at https://GLAOPDC.moderngov.co.uk/documents/s63208/06-0-annex-1-opdc-treasury-management-strategy-2026-27-draft.pdf.
officer.hook: balance-sheet identity ties four-for-four across the horizon (§3.1); the paper's own §2.8 market quote sits 65bp above MUFG's Jun-26 central case at Table 1 (45bp on certainty); paper transparently prints both views side by side and does not attempt to reconcile them
